headline: Fusing structure, sequence and embedding inputs for TCR, BCR and MHC-peptide binding
label: Multimodal Biomedical Prediction Models
summary: Recent reports pair predicted structures, pretrained embeddings and generative augmentation with graph networks for immune-recognition prediction.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is multimodal input construction for immune-molecule binding prediction, where learned representations are combined with structural or sequence-derived features. TCRLens uses an equivariant graph neural network with VAE-GAN augmentation to predict TCR-pMHC-I recognition from structure, and IgPose pairs generative data augmentation with equivariant GNNs and ESM-2 embeddings to score immunoglobulin-antigen poses. CMHS fuses ESM2 sequence embeddings and BLOSUM50 features with a heterogeneous subgraph network for MHC-peptide binding affinity. CoMBCR co-learns BCR sequences and gene expression in a shared latent space and is reported to outperform BCR-only encoders. The TCR-pMHC preprint examines why GNN classifiers trained on predicted structures generalize poorly to unseen peptides. What is new relative to single-modality encoders is the explicit coupling of structural graphs, language-model embeddings and generative augmentation, evaluated against sequence-only or single-modality baselines.
